l-m-e4-b01-01.title: If di ten-thousands digit no be 0, e dey always be five-digit number?
l-m-e4-b01-01.topic: Five-digit numbers and di ten-thousands place
l-m-e4-b01-01.goal: Check whether di claim say number na five-digit number anytime im ten-thousands digit no be 0 dey always true, then find and explain one case wey no true (a counterexample).
l-m-e4-b01-01.material: Claim: If di ten-thousands digit of number no be 0, di number go always be five-digit number. Find one number wey show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-e4-b01-01.s.s1.r.a: E be five-digit number. Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-e4-b01-01.s.s1.r.c: E be five-digit number. Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-e4-b01-01.s.s1.r.d: E be five-digit number. Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-e4-b01-01.s.s1.explain: 120000 get 2 for di ten-thousands place, but e get hundred-thousands place, so e be six-digit number.
l-m-e4-b01-01.s.s2.model.0: For 120000 di ten-thousands digit na 2, but e be six-digit number. E no be five-digit number, so e be counterexample.
l-m-e4-b01-01.s.s2.model.1: Even if di ten-thousands digit no be 0, number wey get hundred-thousands place na six-digit number, so 120000 na counterexample.

l-m-e4-b01-09.title: Di product of two two-digit numbers dey always be four-digit number?
l-m-e4-b01-09.goal: Check whether di claim say di product of two two-digit numbers na always four-digit number dey always true, then find and explain one case wey no true (a counterexample).
l-m-e4-b01-09.material: Claim: When you multiply two-digit number by two-digit number, di product na always four-digit number. Find one multiplication wey show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-e4-b01-09.s.s1.r.b: Di product 7448 na four-digit number. Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-e4-b01-09.s.s1.r.c: Di product 1440 na four-digit number. Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-e4-b01-09.s.s1.r.d: Di product 1311 na four-digit number. Na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-e4-b01-09.s.s1.explain: 12×15=180 na three-digit number. If di product small pass 1000, e no be four-digit number.
l-m-e4-b01-09.s.s2.model.0: 12×15=180, and 180 na three-digit number. Di product no be four digits, so e be counterexample.
l-m-e4-b01-09.s.s2.model.1: Even with two-digit numbers, to multiply small ones no reach 1000, so 12×15=180 break di claim.

l-m-e4-b01-17.title: Improper fraction na always number wey big pass 1?
l-m-e4-b01-17.goal: Check whether di claim say improper fraction na always number wey big pass 1 always true, and find and explain one case wey e no true (a counterexample).
l-m-e4-b01-17.material: Claim: Improper fraction na fraction wey im numerator equal or big pass im denominator, and every improper fraction na number wey big pass 1. Find one improper fraction wey show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-e4-b01-17.s.s1.prompt: Choose di improper fraction wey go against di claim (di counterexample).
l-m-e4-b01-17.s.s1.r.a: 11/3 na number wey big pass 1. E be example wey fit di claim.
l-m-e4-b01-17.s.s1.r.b: 9/5 na number wey big pass 1. E be example wey fit di claim.
l-m-e4-b01-17.s.s1.r.c: 7/4 na number wey big pass 1. E be example wey fit di claim.
l-m-e4-b01-17.s.s1.explain: 5/5 na improper fraction, but e equal 1. E no be number wey big pass 1.
l-m-e4-b01-17.s.s2.model.0: 5/5 na improper fraction wey im numerator and denominator na di same, but im value na 1. E no big pass 1, so e be counterexample.
l-m-e4-b01-17.s.s2.model.1: Improper fraction wey im numerator equal im denominator equal 1, so 5/5 break di claim.

l-m-e4-b01-25.goal: Check whether claim more decimal digits means bigger number always true, and find counterexample.
l-m-e4-b01-25.material: Claim: Of two decimals, one with more digits after point is bigger. Find pair against it.
l-m-e4-b01-25.s.s1.r.b: 0.31 bigger and got more places, example supporting claim.
l-m-e4-b01-25.s.s1.r.c: 0.12 bigger and more places, supports claim.
l-m-e4-b01-25.s.s1.r.d: 0.52 bigger and more places, supports claim.
l-m-e4-b01-25.s.s1.explain: 0.75 get more places but less than 0.8=0.80.
l-m-e4-b01-25.s.s2.model.0: 0.75 get 2 decimal places but less than 0.80. More decimal digits no mean bigger.
l-m-e4-b01-25.s.s2.model.1: 0.8 same as 0.80, and bigger than 0.75, so 0.8 and 0.75 disprove claim.

l-m-e4-b01-33.title: If two angles na acute, the one wey remain go be obtuse?
l-m-e4-b01-33.goal: Check if the claim say if two angles na acute, the remaining angle na obtuse dey always true, and find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-e4-b01-33.material: Claim: For triangle, if two angles na acute, the remaining angle must be obtuse. When two angles of triangle be like below, find the case wey the remaining angle no be obtuse.
l-m-e4-b01-33.s.s1.prompt: Choose the two angles wey go against the claim (counterexample).
l-m-e4-b01-33.s.s1.r.a: The remaining angle na 110°, wey be obtuse, so e be example wey follow the claim.
l-m-e4-b01-33.s.s1.r.c: The remaining angle na 110°, wey be obtuse, so e be example wey follow the claim.
l-m-e4-b01-33.s.s1.r.d: The remaining angle na 110°, wey be obtuse, so e be example wey follow the claim.
l-m-e4-b01-33.s.s1.explain: 50°+60°=110°, so the remaining angle na 70°, wey be acute. Na triangle wey all im three angles na acute.
l-m-e4-b01-33.s.s2.model.0: 180°−50°−60°=70°, and 70° na acute, so the remaining angle no be obtuse. Na so e take become counterexample.
l-m-e4-b01-33.s.s2.model.1: If the sum of the two acute angles pass 90°, the remaining angle small pass 90°, so 50° and 60° break the claim.

l-m-e4-b02-01.title: If you add one 0, e dey always make number 10 times as big?
l-m-e4-b02-01.topic: To add 0 to the end of number
l-m-e4-b02-01.goal: Check if the claim say to add 0 to the end of number go make am 10 times as big dey always true, and find and explain one case wey e no true (counterexample).
l-m-e4-b02-01.material: Claim: If you add one 0 to the right end of number, that number go always become 10 times as big. Find one case wey show say this claim wrong.
l-m-e4-b02-01.s.s1.r.a: 4000 na 10 times 400, so e be example wey follow the claim.
l-m-e4-b02-01.s.s1.r.c: 250 na 10 times 25, so e be example wey follow the claim.
l-m-e4-b02-01.s.s1.r.d: 70 na 10 times 7, so e be example wey follow the claim.
l-m-e4-b02-01.s.s1.explain: 3.50 na the same number as 3.5. 0 wey dem add to the end of decimal no dey change im size.
l-m-e4-b02-01.s.s2.model.0: 3.50, wey dem make by adding 0 to 3.5, na the same number as 3.5, so e no become 10 times as big. Na so e take become counterexample.
l-m-e4-b02-01.s.s2.model.1: For decimals, to add 0 for the end dey leave the value the same, so 3.5 and 3.50 break the claim.

l-m-e4-b02-09.title: If di number wey dem dey divide big pass, di quotient big pass?
l-m-e4-b02-09.goal: Check whether di claim say di bigger di number wey dem dey divide, di bigger di quotient dey always true, then find and explain one case wey no true (a counterexample).
l-m-e4-b02-09.material: Claim: Even when di divisors different, di division wey get bigger number wey dem dey divide go always get bigger quotient. Compare two divisions and find di pair wey show say dis claim wrong.
l-m-e4-b02-09.s.s1.r.b: Di quotients na 20 and 21, and 84÷4 big pass, so na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-e4-b02-09.s.s1.r.c: Di quotients na 30 and 50, and 150÷3 big pass, so na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-e4-b02-09.s.s1.r.d: Di quotients na 20 and 24, and 120÷5 big pass, so na example wey fit di claim.
l-m-e4-b02-09.s.s1.explain: 300 big pass 200, but 300÷30=10 and 200÷4=50, so di quotient small pass.
l-m-e4-b02-09.s.s2.model.0: 300 big pass 200, but di quotient 300÷30=10 small pass 200÷4=50, so e be counterexample.
l-m-e4-b02-09.s.s2.model.1: When di divisor grow to 30, di quotient shrink, so 300÷30, wey get bigger number wey dem dey divide, break di claim.

l-m-e4-b02-17.material: Claim: Quadrilateral wey all four sides get the same length na always square. See quadrilaterals wey get four sides of the same length. Find the one wey show say this claim wrong.
l-m-e4-b02-17.s.s1.o.a: Side na 7 cm, all four angles na right angles
l-m-e4-b02-17.s.s1.r.a: E be square. E be example wey match the claim.
l-m-e4-b02-17.s.s1.r.b: E be square. E be example wey match the claim.

l-m-e4-b02-17.s.s1.o.c: Side na 6 cm, one angle na 70°
l-m-e4-b02-17.s.s1.o.d: Side na 3 cm, all four angles na right angles
l-m-e4-b02-17.s.s1.r.d: All four angles na right angles, so e be square. E be example wey match the claim.
l-m-e4-b02-17.s.s1.explain: Even if the four sides equal, if one angle na 70°, e be rhombus wey no get right angles. E no be square.

l-m-e4-b02-25.title: If you add proper fractions, the sum go always be proper fraction?
l-m-e4-b02-25.goal: Check whether di claim say when you add proper fractions di sum na proper fraction always na true, then find and explain one case wey no be so (counterexample).
l-m-e4-b02-25.material: Claim: If you add two proper fractions wey get di same denominator, di sum na always proper fraction. Find di addition wey show say dis claim no correct.
l-m-e4-b02-25.s.s1.r.a: Di sum 3/5 na proper fraction. Na example wey match di claim.
l-m-e4-b02-25.s.s1.r.b: Di sum 7/8 na proper fraction. Na example wey match di claim.
l-m-e4-b02-25.s.s1.r.d: Di sum 5/7 na proper fraction. Na example wey match di claim.
l-m-e4-b02-25.s.s1.explain: 3/5+4/5=7/5 get numerator wey big pass di denominator, so na improper fraction. E no be proper fraction.
l-m-e4-b02-25.s.s2.model.0: 3/5+4/5=7/5, and 7/5 na improper fraction wey im numerator big pass im denominator, so na counterexample.
l-m-e4-b02-25.s.s2.model.1: If di numerator of di sum big pass di denominator, e no be proper fraction, so 3/5+4/5, wey make 7/5, break di claim.

l-m-e4-b04-07.s.s1.r.a: Di numerator big pass di denominator, so if you divide dis way, di quotient go be 0.
l-m-e4-b04-07.s.s1.o.b: Di product of di denominator and di numerator
l-m-e4-b04-07.s.s1.r.b: Di product no fit tell you how many groups dey.
l-m-e4-b04-07.s.s1.o.c: Di sum of di denominator and di numerator
l-m-e4-b04-07.s.s1.r.c: Di sum no fit tell you di whole-number part.
l-m-e4-b04-07.s.s1.o.d: Di quotient and remainder when you divide di numerator by di denominator
l-m-e4-b04-07.s.s1.explain: 7÷4=1 remainder 3. Di quotient 1 na di whole-number part and di remainder 3 na di numerator, so e become 1 and 3/4.
l-m-e4-b04-07.s.s2.model.0: Di quotient 1 of 7 divided by 4 na di whole-number part, and di remainder 3 become di numerator. Di other choices no fit tell you di whole-number part.
l-m-e4-b04-07.s.s2.model.1: You must know how many times di denominator 4 enter di numerator 7 and how much remain, so you need di quotient and di remainder.

l-m-e4-b04-08.title: How many boxes dem need for di books?
l-m-e4-b04-08.topic: How to use di remainder for division
l-m-e4-b04-08.goal: Decide which criterion (information) you must get to find di number of boxes wey fit hold all di class library books, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-e4-b04-08.material: We wan put 346 class library books inside boxes, 25 books for each box. Find out how many boxes dem need to hold all di books.
l-m-e4-b04-08.s.s1.prompt: Which values you must look to decide di number of boxes?
l-m-e4-b04-08.s.s1.r.a: You fit find di number of boxes by dividing, no be by multiplying.
l-m-e4-b04-08.s.s1.r.b: If you look only di quotient 13, box no dey for di 21 books wey remain.
l-m-e4-b04-08.s.s1.o.c: Di quotient and di remainder of 346÷25
l-m-e4-b04-08.s.s1.r.d: Dem don already decide say each box dey hold 25 books, so dem no need di size.
l-m-e4-b04-08.s.s1.explain: 346÷25=13 remainder 21. Dem must also pack di 21 books wey remain, so di number of boxes na 13+1=14.
l-m-e4-b04-08.s.s2.model.0: Di quotient 13 na di number of full boxes, and 21 books remain, so dem need one more box. Dat one make 14.
l-m-e4-b04-08.s.s2.model.1: If you look only di quotient, 21 books remain, so you must look di remainder too. When remainder dey, you go use one more box.

l-m-e4-b04-09.title: How you fit see for one look di number of boys wey dey wear glasses?
l-m-e4-b04-09.goal: Decide which criterion (information) you must get to know di number of boys wey dey wear glasses, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-e4-b04-09.material: We do survey of di gender and glasses-wearing of di 24 students for our class. We wan make table wey we fit use find sharp sharp how many boys dey wear glasses.
l-m-e4-b04-09.s.s1.prompt: How dem go divide di table?
l-m-e4-b04-09.s.s1.r.a: If you divide by gender only, you no fit know how many people dey wear glasses.
l-m-e4-b04-09.s.s1.o.b: Divide by whether dem dey wear glasses only
l-m-e4-b04-09.s.s1.r.b: If you divide by glasses only, you no fit know whether dem be boys.
l-m-e4-b04-09.s.s1.r.c: Di number order no hold gender or glasses information.
l-m-e4-b04-09.s.s1.o.d: Divide by gender and glasses-wearing together
l-m-e4-b04-09.s.s1.explain: If you divide di cells by two criteria, gender and glasses, you fit read di number for di cell of boys wey dey wear glasses sharp sharp.
l-m-e4-b04-09.s.s2.model.0: Because you must divide by both criteria together to find di cell for boys wey dey wear glasses. If you divide by only one, you no fit know both conditions.
l-m-e4-b04-09.s.s2.model.1: If you divide by gender only, you leave out di glasses information, and if you divide by glasses only, you leave out di gender information, so you must use both criteria together.

l-m-e4-b04-10.title: Di criterion to know slide from turn
l-m-e4-b04-10.goal: Decide which criterion (information) you must get to know whether dem slide or turn one figure, then explain why you choose am.
l-m-e4-b04-10.material: Dem move one figure for grid one time and now e dey for different place. Im size remain di same. We wan know whether dem slide am or dem turn am.
l-m-e4-b04-10.s.s1.prompt: Wetin you must check to know di difference?
l-m-e4-b04-10.s.s1.o.a: Di size of di figure change?
l-m-e4-b04-10.s.s1.r.a: Di size dey remain di same for both sliding and turning.
l-m-e4-b04-10.s.s1.o.b: Di position of di figure change?
l-m-e4-b04-10.s.s1.r.b: Di position fit change for both sliding and turning.
l-m-e4-b04-10.s.s1.o.c: Di direction wey di figure dey face change?
l-m-e4-b04-10.s.s1.o.d: Di name of di figure change?
l-m-e4-b04-10.s.s1.r.d: Di name of figure no dey change when e move.
l-m-e4-b04-10.s.s1.explain: When you slide, di shape and direction remain di same and only di position dey change. When you turn, di direction dey change.
l-m-e4-b04-10.s.s2.model.0: Sliding dey keep di direction di same and turning dey change di direction, so you must check whether di direction change.
l-m-e4-b04-10.s.s2.model.1: Size and position fit be di same for both movements, so dem no fit be di criterion to know di difference. You must check di direction.

l-m-e4-b05-06.material: You wan find all the octagons among different polygons. Without looking the pictures of the shapes, decide which criterion to use to separate dem.
l-m-e4-b05-06.s.s1.o.a: All the sides get the same length?
l-m-e4-b05-06.s.s1.r.a: Sides wey get the same length na criterion for regular polygon.
l-m-e4-b05-06.s.s1.o.c: All the angles na right angles?
l-m-e4-b05-06.s.s1.r.c: If all the angles na right angles, only shapes like rectangles go remain.
l-m-e4-b05-06.s.s1.r.d: How long the perimeter be no get anything to do with the number of sides.
l-m-e4-b05-06.s.s1.explain: Octagon na polygon wey get 8 sides. If you just count the number of sides, you fit know whether e be octagon.
l-m-e4-b05-06.s.s2.model.0: The number of sides decide the name of polygon, so you only need to check whether e get 8 sides.
l-m-e4-b05-06.s.s2.model.1: Whether the sides get the same length or how big the angles be no get anything to do with being octagon, so you must count the sides.

l-m-e4-b05-07.goal: Decide which criterion (information) you must get to find the perimeter of rectangular picture frame, then explain the reason for your choice.
l-m-e4-b05-07.material: You wan go round the edge of rectangular picture frame one time and stick string for am. The length of string wey you need equal the perimeter of the frame.

l-m-e4-b05-07.s.s1.o.b: The length of just one diagonal
l-m-e4-b05-07.s.s1.r.b: One diagonal alone no fit decide the width and height.
l-m-e4-b05-07.s.s1.r.c: Weight no get anything to do with length.

l-m-e4-b05-07.s.s2.model.1: One diagonal alone no fit decide the width and height, so you must get the length and the width.

l-m-e4-b05-08.goal: Decide which criterion (information) you must get to find out whether triangle na acute triangle, then explain the reason for your choice.
l-m-e4-b05-08.material: You wan check whether triangle wey you know all three angles na acute triangle. Acute triangle na triangle wey all three angles na acute angles (angles wey small pass 90°).
l-m-e4-b05-08.s.s1.r.a: The smallest angle small pass 90° for any triangle.
l-m-e4-b05-08.s.s1.o.b: The sum of the three angles na 180°?
l-m-e4-b05-08.s.s1.r.b: The sum na 180° for every triangle, so e no fit separate dem.
l-m-e4-b05-08.s.s1.r.d: Whether two angles equal na criterion about isosceles triangles.
l-m-e4-b05-08.s.s1.explain: If the biggest angle small pass 90°, the other angles na acute too. You only need to check the biggest angle.
l-m-e4-b05-08.s.s2.model.0: If the biggest angle small pass 90°, the other angles all small pass 90° too, so na acute triangle.
l-m-e4-b05-08.s.s2.model.1: The smallest angle and the sum of the three angles always give the same result, so dem no fit separate triangles. You need to look the biggest angle.

l-m-e4-b05-09.title: How you go find the color of the 25th bead?
l-m-e4-b05-09.goal: Decide which criterion (information) you must get to find the 25th color for repeating string of beads, then explain the reason for your choice.
l-m-e4-b05-09.material: Dem string beads for this order: red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue, red… You wan find the color of the 25th bead.
l-m-e4-b05-09.s.s1.o.a: The shape of the group wey dey repeat
l-m-e4-b05-09.s.s1.o.b: Only the color of the first bead
l-m-e4-b05-09.s.s1.r.b: Only the color of the first bead no tell you how e dey repeat.
l-m-e4-b05-09.s.s1.o.c: Only how many red beads dey
l-m-e4-b05-09.s.s1.r.c: If you know only the number of red beads, you no fit find position 25.
l-m-e4-b05-09.s.s1.r.d: Even if you know the total number, you no fit tell the color for position 25.
l-m-e4-b05-09.s.s1.explain: Red, blue, blue dey repeat for groups of 3. 25÷3=8 remainder 1, so the 25th na the first one for the group, red.
l-m-e4-b05-09.s.s2.model.0: Red, blue, blue dey repeat for groups of 3, and 25 na 3×8+1, so the 25th na the 1st for the group, red.
l-m-e4-b05-09.s.s2.model.1: You need to know the length of the group wey dey repeat to find the position with the remainder of 25 divided by 3, so you must get the group.

l-m-e4-b05-10.title: Criterion to sort lines wey their length fit measure
l-m-e4-b05-10.goal: Decide which criterion (information) you must get to find out which lines get length wey dem fit measure, then explain the reason for your choice.
l-m-e4-b05-10.material: Line segment AB, line AB, and ray AB dey. You wan sort dem into the ones wey dem fit measure their length and the ones wey dem no fit measure.
l-m-e4-b05-10.s.s1.prompt: Which one na the correct criterion for sorting?
l-m-e4-b05-10.s.s1.r.a: All three na straight lines, so e no fit separate dem.
l-m-e4-b05-10.s.s1.o.b: Dem name am with two points?
l-m-e4-b05-10.s.s1.r.b: Dem name all three with two points, so e no fit separate dem.
l-m-e4-b05-10.s.s1.o.c: E get endpoints for both sides?
l-m-e4-b05-10.s.s1.o.d: The thickness of the line the same?
l-m-e4-b05-10.s.s1.r.d: Thickness no get anything to do with whether dem fit measure the length.
l-m-e4-b05-10.s.s1.explain: Only line segment get endpoints for both sides, so dem fit measure its length. Line and ray dey stretch without end.
l-m-e4-b05-10.s.s2.model.0: If endpoints dey for both sides, the length don fix, so only line segment dem fit measure. Line and ray dey stretch without end for one side or both sides.
l-m-e4-b05-10.s.s2.model.1: All three lines straight and dem name dem with two points, so whether endpoints dey for both sides na the criterion to measure length.

l-m-e4-b01-35.topic: The sum of the three angles of triangle
l-m-e4-b01-35.goal: Find and talk the pattern for some examples of the sum of the three angles of triangle, then check the pattern with new case.
l-m-e4-b01-35.material: Dem measure the angles of three triangles: 40°, 70°, 70° / 30°, 60°, 90° / 50°, 50°, 80°. Find the pattern for the sum of the three angles.

l-m-e4-b01-35.s.s1.r.c: E write the sum of the two angles, 35°+65°, as the answer just like that.
l-m-e4-b01-35.s.s1.r.d: E guess say the remaining angle na right angle.

l-m-e4-b01-35.s.s2.model.0: For all the three triangles the sum of the three angles na 180°, so the remaining angle na 180°−35°−65°=80°.
l-m-e4-b01-35.s.s2.model.1: The sum dey always be 180°, so if you subtract 100°, wey be 35° plus 65°, from 180° e go give 80°.

l-m-e4-b02-03.title: The pattern of counting by ten-millions
l-m-e4-b02-03.goal: Find and talk the pattern for some examples of counting by ten-millions, then check the pattern with new case.
l-m-e4-b02-03.material: Dem be 5 hundred-million 8 ten-million (580,000,000), 5 hundred-million 9 ten-million (590,000,000), 6 hundred-million (600,000,000), and 6 hundred-million 1 ten-million (610,000,000). Use the pattern of to grow by 1 ten-million each time, find the number wey dey after 7 hundred-million 9 ten-million (790,000,000).
l-m-e4-b02-03.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be the number wey come after 7 hundred-million 9 ten-million (790,000,000)?
l-m-e4-b02-03.s.s1.r.a: Dem add only 1 ten-thousand. You must add 1 ten-million.
l-m-e4-b02-03.s.s1.r.b: When di ten-millions place go from 9 reach 10, e dey carry go di hundred-millions place.
l-m-e4-b02-03.s.s1.r.d: Na di number wey dem count one more time.
l-m-e4-b02-03.s.s1.explain: To add 1 ten-million to 7 hundred-million 9 ten-million make di ten-millions place 10, so e be 8 hundred-million.
l-m-e4-b02-03.s.s2.model.0: Di pattern dey grow by 1 ten-million each time, so to add 1 ten-million to 7 hundred-million 9 ten-million make 8 hundred-million.
l-m-e4-b02-03.s.s2.model.1: To add 1 to di 9 for di ten-millions place cause carry, so di hundred-millions place go up by one and e become 8 hundred-million.

l-m-e4-b02-11.s.s2.model.1: Di remainder na 0 for multiples of 5 like 15, and di numbers wey come after na 1, 2, so di remainder of 47, wey come after 45, na 2.

l-m-e4-b02-19.goal: Find and talk the rule from plenty cases of the number of triangles wey polygon divide into, then check the rule with one new case.
l-m-e4-b02-19.material: If you draw diagonals from one vertex to divide polygon into triangles, quadrilateral give 2, pentagon give 3, and hexagon give 4. How many triangles go heptagon divide into?

l-m-e4-b02-19.s.s1.r.a: 4 na the number wey hexagon divide into.
l-m-e4-b02-19.s.s1.r.c: 7 na the number of sides for heptagon.
l-m-e4-b02-19.s.s1.r.d: 6 na the number wey octagon divide into.
l-m-e4-b02-19.s.s1.explain: E be the number of sides minus 2. For heptagon, e be 7−2=5.
l-m-e4-b02-19.s.s2.model.0: Quadrilateral give 2, pentagon give 3, and hexagon give 4, each one dey 2 less than the number of sides, so heptagon give 7−2=5.
l-m-e4-b02-19.s.s2.model.1: Every time the polygon get 1 more side, 1 more triangle dey add, so after the hexagon wey get 4, the heptagon get 5.

l-m-e4-b03-19.title: Di base angle rule of isosceles triangle
l-m-e4-b03-19.goal: Find and talk one rule from several cases of di apex angle and base angles of isosceles triangle, then check di rule with new case.

l-m-e4-b03-19.s.s2.model.1: The rule na to comot the apex angle from 180° and divide by two, so (180°−30°)÷2=75°.

l-m-e4-b0s2-01.goal: Estimate the temperature at 4 p.m., wey no dey the graph, decide on suitable size or range, then explain your reasoning.
l-m-e4-b0s2-01.material: One greenhouse measure 24°C at 3 p.m. and 12°C at 6 p.m. For line graph, dem join the two points with line segment. Dem no measure the temperature at 4 p.m.
l-m-e4-b0s2-01.s.s1.prompt: Which one na the best estimate of the temperature at 4 p.m.?
l-m-e4-b0s2-01.s.s1.r.a: E use the value of the point wey near as e be. The line segment dey go down continuously.
l-m-e4-b0s2-01.s.s1.r.c: E treat 4 o'clock as the middle of 3 and 6 o'clock. The middle na 4:30.
l-m-e4-b0s2-01.s.s1.r.d: E use the value for 6 o'clock. 4 o'clock near 3 o'clock pass 6 o'clock.
l-m-e4-b0s2-01.s.s1.explain: E fall 12°C for 3 hours, so e dey fall 4°C every hour. At 4 o'clock e be about 24−4=20°C.
l-m-e4-b0s2-01.s.s2.model.0: E fall 12°C for 3 hours, so e dey fall 4°C every hour. So at 4 o'clock e be about 24−4=20°C.
l-m-e4-b0s2-01.s.s2.model.1: 4 o'clock na one hour after 3 o'clock, so e don fall one third (1/3) of the whole 3 hours, wey be about 20°C.

l-m-e4-b01-37.s.s1.r.d: Na the result of to follow the mistake for ①.
l-m-e4-b01-37.s.s1.explain: The sum of the three angles of triangle na 180°. 180°−115°=65° na the remaining angle.

l-m-e4-b04-22.material: Solution to 275÷25: ① 25×10=250 ② 275−250=25 ③ 25 na the remainder, so the quotient na 10 and the remainder na 25 ④ Check: 25×10+25=275. Find the first wrong line.
l-m-e4-b04-22.s.s1.r.d: The calculation for the check correct. The remainder na the problem.
l-m-e4-b04-22.s.s1.explain: The remainder must small pass the divisor, 25. Since 25 remain, divide one more time to get quotient of 11 and remainder of 0.
l-m-e4-b04-22.s.s2.model.0: The remainder 25 equal the divisor 25, so you fit divide further, na why ③ wrong. Fix the quotient to 11.
l-m-e4-b04-22.s.s2.model.1: The remainder must small pass the divisor, so 25 no fit remain. 275=25×11, so the remainder na 0.

l-m-e4-b04-23.goal: Follow the solution to how to read the number of students from bar graph, or the chain of cause and effect, step by step, find the first place wey e go wrong, then fix am.

l-m-e4-b04-23.s.s1.r.b: E talk say the height of the bar na 6 steps.

l-m-e4-b04-23.s.s2.model.0: One step na 2 students, so 6 steps must be 2×6=12 students. Na why ③, wey use the number of steps as e be, wrong.
l-m-e4-b04-23.s.s2.model.1: For ③, dem no multiply the value of one step for the scale, 2, so e come out as 6 students. The fix na 12 students.

l-m-e4-b04-24.goal: Follow the process of how to find the base angles of isosceles triangle, or the chain of cause and effect, step by step, find the first place wey e go wrong, then fix am.
l-m-e4-b04-24.material: Solution for the base angle of isosceles triangle wey him apex angle na 30°: ① The sum of the three angles na 180° ② 180°−30°=150° ③ The two base angles equal, so one base angle na 150° ④ The base angle na 150°. Find the first wrong line.
l-m-e4-b04-24.s.s1.o.a: ① The sum of the three angles na 180°
l-m-e4-b04-24.s.s1.r.a: E correct say the sum of the three angles of triangle na 180°.
l-m-e4-b04-24.s.s1.explain: 150° na the sum of the two base angles. The two base angles equal, so one base angle na 150°÷2=75°.
l-m-e4-b04-24.s.s2.model.0: 150° na the size of the two base angles put together, so dem must split am into two as 75° each, na why ③ wrong.
l-m-e4-b04-24.s.s2.model.1: 75°+75°+30°=180°, so the base angle na 75° and 150° wrong.

l-m-e4-b05-22.goal: Follow di steps of di solution, or di chain of cause and effect, for how to find di perimeter of parallelogram one by one, find di first place wey e go wrong, then fix am.
l-m-e4-b05-22.material: Solution for di perimeter of parallelogram wey im two neighboring sides na 8 cm and 5 cm: ① Opposite sides get di same length. ② Di sum of di two neighboring sides na 8+5=13. ③ Di perimeter na 13 cm. Find di first wrong line.

l-m-e4-b05-22.s.s2.model.1: Opposite sides equal, so 8+5+8+5=26 cm, but ③ add only two sides, so e wrong.

l-m-e4-b05-25.title: To check solution wey change sum of fractions to mixed number
l-m-e4-b05-25.goal: Follow di steps of di solution, or di chain of cause and effect, for di calculation of 5/9+7/9 one by one, find di first place wey e go wrong, then fix am.
l-m-e4-b05-25.material: Solution of 5/9+7/9: ① Di denominators na di same, so di denominator remain 9. ② Add di numerators: 5+7=12. ③ For 12/9, comot di whole number 1 and write am as 1 and 12/9. ④ Di answer na 1 and 12/9. Find di first wrong line.
l-m-e4-b05-25.s.s1.r.a: When di denominators na di same, e correct to leave di denominator as e be.
l-m-e4-b05-25.s.s1.r.d: ④ na di result wey come from di wrong expression for ③.
l-m-e4-b05-25.s.s1.explain: If you comot 1 (=9/9) from 12/9, di numerator remain 12−9=3. So di answer na 1 and 3/9.
l-m-e4-b05-25.s.s2.model.0: When you comot 1, you must remove 9 from di numerator 12, so 12/9 become 1 and 3/9, but ③ wrongly keep 12 as e be.
l-m-e4-b05-25.s.s2.model.1: 1 and 12/9 na bigger number wey add 12/9 to 1 again, so e different from 5/9+7/9=12/9. So fix am to 1 and 3/9.

l-m-e4-b01-15.title: To compare two solutions of 630÷30
l-m-e4-b01-15.topic: Two ways to solve a division
l-m-e4-b01-15.goal: Compare di two methods or claims for how to solve 630÷30, choose di one wey better, and explain why you choose am.
l-m-e4-b01-15.material: Method A: From 63÷3=21, add one 0, so di quotient na 210. Method B: 30×20=600, and di remaining 30 na 30×1, so di quotient na 21.
l-m-e4-b01-15.s.s1.prompt: Which method fit when you check am?
l-m-e4-b01-15.s.s1.r.c: Di quotients, 210 and 21, differ, so both no fit correct.
l-m-e4-b01-15.s.s1.explain: 30×21=630, so di quotient na 21. When you divide after you cross out 0s, you no dey add 0 to di quotient.

l-m-e4-b04-32.material: Two people talk different things about which big pass, di improper fraction 7/3 or di mixed number 2 and 2/3. A: 7 big pass 2, so 7/3 big pass. B: You must change 7/3 to mixed number before you compare.
l-m-e4-b04-32.s.s1.prompt: For di two statements, which one get reason wey fit and correct conclusion?

l-m-e4-b04-32.s.s1.r.c: If you change am to mixed number, you fit compare dem.
l-m-e4-b04-32.s.s1.o.d: B: 7/3=2 and 1/3, so 2 and 2/3 big pass
l-m-e4-b04-32.s.s1.explain: 7/3 na 2 and 1/3. Di whole-number parts dey di same and 1/3 small pass 2/3, so 2 and 2/3 big pass.
l-m-e4-b04-32.s.s2.model.0: If you change 7/3 to mixed number, e go be 2 and 1/3, and 1/3 small pass 2/3, so 2 and 2/3 big pass.
l-m-e4-b04-32.s.s2.model.1: Di numerator 7 and di 2 na numbers wey get different meaning, so you no fit compare dem directly. If you change dem to di same form, 2 and 2/3 big pass.

l-m-e4-b02-32.material: Pour 3 L of juice inside 8 cups for equal amounts. Conditions: each cup dey for steps of 0.05 L, at least 0.25 L and at most 0.4 L, di juice must no pass 3 L, and pour as much as possible.
